source_path_analysis: Each task uses subprocess.run with timeout=TASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
TimeoutExpired returns a result object containing only error=task_wall_timeout and no results list.
The aggregation first increments the task_wall_timeout counter, then independently increments result_count_mismatch because results is absent or has the wrong length.
Therefore result_count_mismatch overlaps task_wall_timeout and must not be added to it as a second set of failed tasks.
conclusion: The apparent 8 and 12 combined error counts are double counting. The observed runs had 4 and 6 unique timeout tasks respectively.
The number of timed out tasks varied by two between runs, but the generated submission bytes were identical.
The audit did not persist task IDs for worker failures, so which tasks timed out and why they crossed the limit remain UNKNOWN.
No production code change is justified by this aggregate-only diagnostic; the emitted HDS candidates still show zero additive pass@2 gains.
